claims.claim: The Home Depot is the world’s largest home improvement retailer and offers a wide assortment of home improvement, building materials, lawn and garden, décor and facilities MRO products in stores and online.
claims.quote: The Home Depot, Inc. is the world’s largest home improvement retailer based on net sales for fiscal 2025. We offer our customers a wide assortment of home improvement products, building materials, lawn and garden products, décor products, and facilities MRO products, in stores and online.

claims.claim: The company serves both DIY customers who implement projects themselves and professional customers – including contractors, tradespeople and specialty renovators – who undertake complex residential and commercial projects.
claims.quote: These customers are primarily professional renovators/remodelers, general contractors, homebuilders, maintenance professionals, handymen, property managers, building service contractors and specialty tradespeople, such as electricians, landscapers, insulation installers, plumbers, painters, pool contractors, roofers, and wallboard and ceiling installers.

claims.claim: The industry is described as highly competitive, highly fragmented and evolving.
claims.quote: Our industry is highly competitive, highly fragmented, and evolving.

claims.claim: The Home Depot leverages brand strength, customer service, product authority, scale, real‑estate footprint, digital and interconnected experiences and deep professional relationships to capture growth in fragmented markets.
claims.quote: The Home Depot is focused on leveraging its distinct competitive advantages – our brand, excellent customer service, product authority in home improvement, knowledgeable associates and culture, scale, premier real estate portfolio, digital and interconnected experience, supply chain network, and our deep relationships with Pros – to take advantage of the significant growth opportunities in the highly fragmented markets in which we operate.

claims.claim: In fiscal 2025 the company invested heavily in capital projects to support its growth strategy.
claims.quote: In fiscal 2025, we invested $3.7 billion in capital expenditures across initiatives supporting our strategy of driving our core and culture, including building new stores and maintaining existing stores, delivering a frictionless, interconnected experience, and winning with Pros.

claims.claim: The firm has a multi‑year plan to open dozens of new stores to relieve pressure on high‑traffic locations and capture market voids.
claims.quote: In fiscal 2023, we initiated a plan to open approximately 80 new stores over a five-year period to address those opportunities, and in fiscal 2025, we opened 12 new stores.

claims.claim: The Home Depot is investing in artificial‑intelligence‑driven tools such as Magic ApronTM and Blueprint Takeoffs to improve search, recommendations, chat and project‑specific material list generation.
claims.quote: In addition to supporting our DIY and DIFM customers, we also invest in AI tools to improve our search, recommendations, and chat features, and offering new AI-powered customer-facing tools such as Magic ApronTM, which supports customers and associates with online product and project inquiries, and our AI-powered Blueprint Takeoffs Tool and Material List Builder, which generate project-specific materials lists and quotes.

claims.claim: Both in‑store and online competition is based on experience, price, quality, availability, assortment, innovation and delivery capabilities.
claims.quote: Both in-store and online, we compete primarily based on customer experience; price; quality; product availability, assortment, and innovation; and delivery options and capabilities.

claims.claim: The company’s strategic acquisitions of SRS and subsequently GMS expanded its specialty‑trade distribution footprint across roofing, landscape, pool and interior building products.
claims.quote: In fiscal 2024, we acquired SRS, a leading residential specialty trade distribution company across several verticals engaged in the distribution of residential and commercial roofing products and complementary building products, landscape supplies, and swimming pool supplies serving the professional roofer, landscaper, and pool contractor. In fiscal 2025, SRS completed the acquisition of GMS, a leading distributor of specialty building products, including drywall, ceilings, steel framing and other complementary construction products.

claims.claim: The supply‑chain network includes a “ship from best location” algorithm that routes orders to the optimal fulfillment node to enhance speed, reliability, cost and capacity.
claims.quote: Our 'ship from best location' initiative seeks to optimize delivery speed, reliability, cost, and capacity by leveraging machine learning algorithms to route orders to the optimal fulfillment node.

claims.claim: Risk disclosures highlight that strong competition could pressure pricing, demand and market share.
claims.quote: Strong competition could adversely affect prices and demand for our products and services and could decrease our market share.

gaps: The 10‑K does not provide forward‑looking quantitative guidance for fiscal 2026 sales growth, gross margin or operating margin, so any claim about specific percentage targets cannot be sourced.

The earnings release provides quarterly sales and earnings figures, but the 10‑K does not contain a comparable quarterly narrative; therefore, no claim linking the release numbers to the 10‑K narrative can be made.
